Where do my notes live?

Your notes are stored locally on your device. Lattice is a fictional local-first notebook, designed around keeping your research on the device you use.

Can I take my notes to another app?

Yes. Export your notes as Markdown files, a portable text format you can open in a text editor or bring into another app that supports Markdown.

How do I back up my research?

Export your notes as files and keep copies in a backup location you control. Lattice does not promise automatic cloud backup; regularly exporting files is how you make a backup.

What happens if I cancel?

Cancellation has no effect on files you have already exported. Those files remain with you and can be opened independently of Lattice.

designReview.method: Single qualitative review of actual captured desktop and mobile pixels. No numerical aesthetic score.

observations.observation: A large sans-serif headline with an italic serif phrase occupies the left hero column, while a tilted notebook window fills the right. The supporting paragraph and single dark primary action follow a clear vertical order.
observations.implication: The page makes the proposition and its product illustration easy to distinguish, with one obvious primary action.

observations.observation: The sans/italic-serif pairing repeats in section headings. Warm off-white surfaces, charcoal text and a restrained burnt-orange accent recur in tabs, arrows, headings and small labels. The pricing band inverts the base into a dark surface.
observations.implication: The typographic contrast reads as a deliberate system rather than unrelated fonts, and the palette remains coordinated across states.

observations.observation: The hero notebook shows a sidebar, note, highlighted passage, source attachment and linked question. A visible caption calls it an illustrative workspace rather than a live application. The Connect state presents search results with highlighted matching phrases.
observations.implication: The previews explain notebook concepts concretely while clearly limiting what the illustration claims to implement.

observations.observation: Workflow steps and FAQ text are visibly substantial and separated by generous space. Pricing amounts are large with adjacent yearly labels. Several small monospace section labels and fine-print captions are much finer than the body copy.
observations.implication: The main information is easy to find, while decorative metadata and qualifications require closer reading.

observations.observation: The mobile headline occupies several large lines, followed by a long paragraph and primary button. The first viewport contains no notebook preview, only the introductory caption of that next visual area near the bottom. The header’s fictional-demo pill uses very small text.
observations.implication: The mobile opening emphasizes the headline but delays seeing the product. A shorter heading block or tighter opening rhythm would expose the illustration sooner; the visible primary text itself is not overlapped or clipped.

observations.observation: The two yearly plans are visually comparable, but their lists largely repeat the same notebook capabilities. The Studio card explicitly says additional capabilities are not specified.
observations.implication: The presentation avoids inventing an unsupported premium feature, but it also leaves the practical reason for the more expensive tier unresolved. This is a content limitation visible in the artifact, not a numerical design score.

mobileLayoutObservation.note: The width values come from the capture receipt; they are not an aesthetic score.

limits: Only the supplied captured states were reviewed. Mobile coverage here is the initial viewport, not a complete mobile walkthrough.
Static viewport captures do not establish keyboard behavior, motion quality, all responsive states or measured color-contrast conformance.
Visual appearance does not reveal the generating agent’s planning, tool choices, verification method or experimental condition. Process evidence belongs in a separate analysis.
Some anchored captures begin partway through surrounding content; that is real viewport framing, not proof that the candidate clips that content.
The notebook mockups illustrate a fictional product and are not evidence of a functioning notebook application.
No condition mapping was inspected, no source artifact was edited and no numerical aesthetic score, universal winner or causal improvement claim is assigned.

processReview.summary: The Fabius landing run used DOM measurements to locate mobile overflow, constrained the artwork and retested before broadening coverage.

observations.observed: A public outline separated content/styling from keyboard, billing, FAQ and no-JavaScript verification before implementation.
The design reference was read. When the first 360px check failed, an inline browser probe collected element bounding boxes to locate overflow.
A source edit clipped decorative orbit artwork after the overflow failure; the verifier then exited successfully. Subsequent header changes were followed by another expanded browser run.
The later checks add intermediate widths, nested hosting and token contrast calculations; screenshots, script and prototype/Chrome limits were retained.

limits: The initial layout failed a required mobile overflow check despite the supplied design instructions.
A successful candidate-authored Chrome suite is not cross-engine or physical-device validation.
Reference access and successful correction are observed; no individual rule’s causal effect is established.
This descriptive process audit was requested after outcomes existed. It is retrospective and exploratory, not a preregistered process endpoint.
The methods reviewer knows condition assignments; this review is not blinded. Separate proof/design reviewers have their own blinding procedures.
Only public progress messages, observable tool actions, check exits and retained artifact evidence are summarized. No hidden reasoning is inferred or published.
There is no process score, tool-call leaderboard or causal claim. More messages, calls, checks or elapsed time do not imply a better process.
The baseline retains native Codex instructions and the same common trial directions. It is not an unstructured or instruction-free model.
Delegation, external services and auxiliary model calls were prohibited for both conditions. Full orchestration, provider selection, collaboration and autonomous end-to-end deployment are unmeasured.
Treatment includes three or four pinned contracts plus a repository snapshot. Observed behavior cannot be assigned to an individual Fabius rule from this design.
Candidate-authored tests and self-reported passes are process evidence, not substitutes for the independent acceptance and proof checks.
Coverage includes all 12 finalized valid runs from the planned three-task, two-condition, two-repeat study. The two preserved setup attempts are documented separately.
